findings.issue_text: [BUG] `sed -i '' -E` is BSD/macOS sed syntax; on GNU sed (Linux) the empty-string argument is consumed as the sed script and the substitution expression is treated as a filename, so the edit never executes. On any Linux machine the script prints "sed: can't read s|^GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL=...|...|: No such file or directory", and because the script has no `set -e` it continues and prints "✅ Updated GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL in ../.env" — the developer believes the tunnel URL was written while the .env file is byte-for-byte unchanged, and the local Google webhook test silently runs against a stale URL. The repo's own setup-env.sh branches on OSTYPE for exactly this sed incompatibility, so this script breaks the established cross-platform convention.

[BUG] ENV_FILE is the CWD-relative path `../.env`, which resolves to the repository's .env only when the script is invoked from inside the scripts/ directory; invoked the natural way from the repo root (`./scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh`) it points at the directory above the checkout. Run from the repo root, the script `touch`-creates `<repo-parent>/.env` and writes GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL into a file no process reads, while still printing the ✅ success message (line 73); the dev server never receives the tunnel URL, Google channel registrations keep pointing at the previous value, and the developer gets zero error output explaining why webhook testing doesn't work — plus a stray .env file is left polluting the parent directory.

[BUG] The script executes `tmole`, an external npm CLI that is not a dependency anywhere in the repo, with no `command -v tmole` precondition check, and redirects the command's stderr into /tmp/tmole.log so a missing binary produces no visible error. On a fresh clone without `npm i -g tunnelmole`, the script spends 10 seconds printing "Waiting for tmole to initialize..." and then fails with the misleading "❌ Failed to extract Tunnelmole URL." — the actual "command not found" message is buried in /tmp/tmole.log, so the developer never learns that installing Tunnelmole is the prerequisite for running this script at all.

[ADVISORY] The availability path now unconditionally issues `SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {})` — an empty-payload UPDATE whose only effect is bumping SelectedCalendar.updatedAt, a field nothing in this PR reads, since the displayed "Last updated" value comes from CalendarCache.updatedAt via getCacheStatusByCredentialIds. Availability checks — the hottest read path in the app, hit on every booking-page slot query for Google-connected users — now carry an extra UPDATE against every SelectedCalendar row under the credential, adding write amplification and WAL churn to maintain a value with no consumer; the PR ships two parallel freshness mechanisms (CalendarCache.updatedAt, which is read and displayed, and SelectedCalendar.updatedAt, which is only written), so the next maintainer must reverse-engineer which one is authoritative. The deletion test passes: removing this call breaks nothing in the diff.

[ADVISORY] The user-with-calendars fetch now selects `updatedAt` and `googleChannelId` (and getConnectedDestinationCalendars.ts lines 21-27 widen the UserWithCalendars Pick to demand them), but no code in this diff — and no existing code touched by it — reads either field. Every getConnectedDestinationCalendars invocation pays for two extra columns that are fetched and dropped, and the widened UserWithCalendars contract forces every future producer of that type to supply fields nothing consumes; whoever builds the next change on this file must keep dead requirements alive. Reverting these two lines together with the Pick additions and the CalendarService write loses no behavior — if this is groundwork for per-calendar sync status it should land with the code that reads it.

[BUG] The credential-not-found/access-denied branch throws a bare `new Error(...)`, which tRPC wraps as INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR (HTTP 500), instead of the 4xx the codebase produces for this condition everywhere else via HttpError({ statusCode: 401/404 }). Any user who confirms the delete dialog after the credential was already disconnected elsewhere (or who probes another user's credentialId) generates a server-side 500 that lands in monitoring/Sentry classified as a server fault rather than a client error; the UI shows the identical generic "Error deleting cache" toast it shows for genuine failures, destroying the 4xx-vs-5xx signal for both operators and the client.

[ADVISORY] The handler re-implements cache deletion with raw `prisma.calendarCache.deleteMany({ where: { credentialId } })`, bypassing `CalendarCacheRepository.deleteManyByCredential` — the abstraction whose mock deliberately no-ops deletion when calendar-cache is disabled — even though this same PR correctly routes the status read through the repository interface (getCacheStatusByCredentialIds added to interface, mock, and implementation). The codebase now has two deletion paths for CalendarCache: any environment running the mock path (calendar-cache disabled, where deletion is intentionally skipped) still performs a hard delete through this endpoint, and a future change to cache storage must find and update a raw prisma call hidden in a tRPC handler or the "Delete cached data" button will silently stop clearing what the status read reports. Calling the repository method here deletes the duplicated logic outright.

[ADVISORY] The new viewer.calendars.deleteCache mutation — a destructive deleteMany gated by a hand-written ownership predicate — and the new CalendarCacheRepository.getCacheStatusByCredentialIds groupBy mapping ship with no test anywhere in the diff, despite the calendar-cache package shipping a repository mock built for exactly this kind of test. A regression in the ownership predicate (e.g., dropping `userId: user.id` from the where clause at line 20) would let any authenticated user wipe another user's cached availability by guessing credential IDs, and nothing in the suite would fail; a field or null-handling slip in getCacheStatusByCredentialIds would surface only as a blank or wrong "Last updated" value in production.

[ADVISORY] The availability method now runs `await SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {})` after the cache-miss branch, issuing an unconditional UPDATE across every SelectedCalendar row under the credential on each availability lookup (cache hit or miss, since the touch sits outside the `if`). Every booking-page availability render for a Google-connected user performs an extra DB write; concurrent visitors checking the same organizer's availability contend on the same SelectedCalendar rows, inflating write load on the hottest read path in the product — and no code in this diff reads SelectedCalendar.updatedAt, so the cost buys nothing user-visible here.

[ADVISORY] deleteCacheHandler re-implements the existing `ICalendarCacheRepository.deleteManyByCredential` operation as a direct `prisma.calendarCache.deleteMany({ where: { credentialId } })`, bypassing the repository layer and its calendar-cache-disabled mock. Deployments running with calendar-cache disabled — the mode CalendarCacheRepositoryMock exists for (its own log says 'Skipping deleteManyByCredential due to calendar-cache being disabled') — still mutate the calendarCache table through this user-facing action, and the two delete implementations can drift: any future scoping added to deleteManyByCredential silently does not apply to the API path.

[ADVISORY] connectedCalendarsHandler instantiates the concrete `new CalendarCacheRepository()` directly instead of going through the mechanism that substitutes CalendarCacheRepositoryMock when calendar-cache is disabled, so the mock's newly added getCacheStatusByCredentialIds is unreachable from its only consumer. In calendar-cache-disabled deployments, the connectedCalendars query — the endpoint backing the entire calendar settings page — now issues a real groupBy against the calendarCache table that the mock exists to shield, violating the skip-when-disabled contract; the mock method added in this same diff is dead code on every runtime path.

[ADVISORY] The diff ships deleteCacheHandler's ownership check, CalendarCacheRepository.getCacheStatusByCredentialIds's groupBy/_max mapping, and updateManyByCredentialId with zero automated verification — scanning the diff, the only test-shaped files are calendar-cache.repository.mock.ts (a hand-written mock) and scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh (a manual tunnel helper), neither of which asserts anything about this logic. A regression that drops `userId: user.id` from the credential lookup ships green, letting any authenticated user wipe other users' cached calendar data by iterating credentialIds; the same blind spot covers the groupBy mapping that decides which credential's 'Last updated' timestamp is displayed.

[ADVISORY] deleteCacheHandler throws a bare `new Error("Credential not found or access denied")` for an expected not-found/no-permission condition instead of a typed TRPCError with a NOT_FOUND/FORBIDDEN code. tRPC converts the unknown error to INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR (500), so a routine client mistake (stale credentialId after a disconnect) is recorded as a server fault in monitoring and the client cannot distinguish 'wrong credential' from a genuine outage.

[ADVISORY] The cache timestamp is formatted with a hardcoded `Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", ...)` inside a component whose strings are otherwise localized via t(). Non-English users see US-formatted dates ('12/31/2025, 3:04 PM') in an otherwise translated settings UI — the localization requirement the diff's own new locale keys exist to serve is silently dropped for the timestamp.

[ADVISORY] The dropdown trigger is an icon-only `<Button variant="icon" StartIcon="ellipsis">` with no aria-label or screen-reader text, leaving the control that gates the destructive delete-cache and disconnect actions without an accessible name. Screen-reader and voice-control users encounter an unnamed 'button' and cannot identify or target it by name, so the newly introduced actions are effectively unannounced to them.

[ADVISORY] `hasCache = isGoogleCalendar && cacheUpdatedAt` makes the entire cache-status affordance render nothing when the credential has no cache rows, so the feature implements only the 'rows exist' state and has no representation for an empty, cleaned, or disabled cache. Google users whose cache is empty, expired-and-purged, or whose deployment has calendar-cache disabled get no 'Cache Status' entry at all and cannot distinguish 'no cached data yet' from 'the feature is broken' — the PR's headline requirement is unobservable for exactly the users most likely to check.

[BUG] The env update uses BSD/macOS-only `sed -i '' -E`, which GNU sed (Linux) parses as an empty script argument and rejects. On Linux dev machines the script fails at the env-update step with a sed error before writing GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL, so the tunnel is up and the script reports success paths, but the app never receives webhooks and the workflow the script automates does not work.

[ADVISORY] The selectedCalendars query now selects `updatedAt` and `googleChannelId` (and getConnectedDestinationCalendars widens its types to advertise them), but no code in this diff reads either field. Every user-with-selected-calendars fetch carries two dead columns to the client, and the CalendarService touch that populates updatedAt has no consumer here — either the consuming UI was omitted from this PR (half-shipped feature) or the extra query fields and the per-availability write are pure overhead.

[ADVISORY] The diff adds an unconditional SelectedCalendar UPDATE (`await SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {})`) to the Google availability-check path that is traceable to no requirement — the cache-status feature sources its timestamp from CalendarCache.updatedAt (getCacheStatusByCredentialIds), and nothing in this diff ever reads SelectedCalendar.updatedAt. Every Google availability check (the hottest query flow in the product — booking page loads and slot fetches) now issues an UPDATE touching all SelectedCalendar rows for the credential; for users with event-type-scoped calendars that is a multi-row write per cache-miss check, adding write load and row-lock contention on SelectedCalendar while the write's output is consumed by nobody — it is leftover first-implementation machinery now redundant with the CalendarCache-based status the UI actually displays.

[BUG] deleteCacheHandler throws a plain `new Error("Credential not found or access denied")` instead of a TRPCError, so tRPC maps the not-found/authorization failure to INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR (HTTP 500). A user confirming 'Yes, delete cache' on a credential they do not own (or one deleted concurrently) triggers a 500-class server fault that pollutes error monitoring and is indistinguishable from a real server bug, while the client can only render the generic 'Error deleting cache' toast with no way to tell 'not yours' from 'broken'.

[BUG] The cache timestamp is formatted with a hardcoded `new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", { dateStyle: "short", timeStyle: "short" })` inside a component that localizes every other user-facing string via useLocale()/t(). Every non-English user sees 'Last updated: 6/15/25, 3:30 PM' in US date format inside an otherwise localized settings UI — the PR adds the new strings to en/common.json precisely so locales can translate them, but the timestamp itself ignores the user's locale, breaking the app's localization invariant for this feature.

[BUG] getCacheStatusByCredentialIds computes the cache status with a prisma.groupBy whose where clause filters only on credentialId and never checks expiresAt, so a credential whose every CalendarCache row has expired still reports a fresh 'Last updated' timestamp. A user or support engineer debugging stale availability is shown 'Cache Status / Last updated: X' plus a delete affordance for a credential whose cache the availability path treats as absent (every lookup misses on expiresAt), so the diagnostic surface this feature exists for misreports whether usable cached data exists.

[ADVISORY] The new auth-scoped deleteCache mutation and the new getCacheStatusByCredentialIds groupBy ship with zero tests — no test in the diff exercises the ownership filter or the status aggregation. The `userId: user.id` filter in the findFirst is the only barrier preventing any authenticated user from wiping another user's cached availability by guessing a credential id (a regression there means silent cross-user cache deletion plus refetch storms against Google's API); nothing in this diff would catch its removal or breakage.

[ADVISORY] The dev:cron script is switched from the pinned `ts-node` dependency to `npx tsx cron-tester.ts` — tooling churn unrelated to the calendar cache status and actions feature this PR claims to deliver. Untraceable tooling change rides inside a feature PR (complicating revert/bisect of the feature), and `npx` resolves tsx at invocation time, downloading from the npm registry when it is absent from the workspace, so `yarn dev:cron` breaks offline or behind a registry-blocking proxy where the previously pinned ts-node worked.

[ADVISORY] A 79-line personal Tunnelmole dev utility is committed into the repo's scripts directory with no traceability to the stated feature (calendar cache status and actions). The repo permanently carries machine-specific developer scaffolding (hardcoded `../.env`, `/tmp/tmole.log`, tunnelmole rate-limit upsell messaging) that reviewers must maintain, and the script is broken on Linux — `sed -i '' -E` on line 68 makes GNU sed treat `''` as an input filename and fail — so it cannot even serve its purpose outside the author's macOS machine.

[ADVISORY] The user repository select now fetches `updatedAt: true` and `googleChannelId: true` on every selectedCalendar lookup (coupled to the widened UserWithCalendars pick in packages/lib/getConnectedDestinationCalendars.ts), but no code in this diff reads either field. Speculative payload expansion: every connectedCalendars response ships two extra columns per selected calendar — including googleChannelId, an internal Google webhook channel identifier now serialized to the client — with no consumer anywhere in the PR; deleting the widening and the two select lines changes no behavior, which is exactly the deletion test this addition fails.

[ADVISORY] The new dropdown re-implements the disconnect flow (viewer.credentials.delete mutation, success/error toasts, confirmation dialog) that the existing DisconnectIntegration component already provides, leaving two parallel implementations of 'remove app' handling in the codebase after this diff swaps only this wrapper's usage. The two implementations already diverge (this copy adds `utils.viewer.apps.integrations.invalidate()` in onSettled), so any future change to disconnect semantics — new cache invalidations, delegation rules, error handling — must be applied in both places or the settings pages where each is used silently behave differently.

[ADVISORY] connectedCalendarsHandler instantiates the concrete prisma-backed `new CalendarCacheRepository()` directly, bypassing the cache-disabled mock that this same diff extends with getCacheStatusByCredentialIds (the mock's implementation exists precisely to keep cache-disabled deployments off the CalendarCache table). The mock branch added in calendar-cache.repository.mock.ts is dead code with no caller, and deployments running with calendar-cache disabled now issue a prisma.groupBy against CalendarCache on every calendars-settings load — the 'cache disabled' abstraction the mock encodes is silently violated on this new read path.

[BUG] SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {}) passes an empty Prisma update payload, which prisma.selectedCalendar.updateMany rejects at runtime (PrismaClientValidationError: "Argument `data` must not be empty"), so the SelectedCalendar.updatedAt touch the comment promises never executes. Every GoogleCalendarService.getAvailability call — every slot-availability lookup for every Google-connected user, on cache-hit and cache-miss paths alike — throws before returning, so booking pages fail to show any availability; the documented touch requires an explicit { updatedAt: new Date() } payload.

[BUG] connectedCalendarsHandler instantiates the concrete `new CalendarCacheRepository()` instead of the runtime selection seam that returns CalendarCacheRepositoryMock when calendar-cache is disabled, making the mock's getCacheStatusByCredentialIds added in this same diff unreachable dead code. Deployments running with calendar-cache disabled now execute a real prisma.calendarCache.groupBy on every connectedCalendars request, breaking the "cache disabled ⇒ no CalendarCache table access" contract the mock exists to enforce, and rows left over from a previously-enabled period resurface a cache-status/delete-cache UI in a deployment where the feature is contractually off.

[ADVISORY] The cache-refresh bookkeeping is placed as an unconditional UPDATE over every SelectedCalendar row of the credential inside getAvailability, overloading SelectedCalendar.updatedAt (previously "row last modified") into "last availability fetch" while duplicating the freshness fact already recorded on CalendarCache.updatedAt — the timestamp the UI actually displays. Once the payload is fixed, every booking-page availability check (the highest-traffic query path, bot traffic included) issues a credential-wide UPDATE per check — write amplification the hot read path never had — and the duplicated SelectedCalendar.updatedAt drifts from CalendarCache.updatedAt while destroying the column's original meaning for any existing consumer.

[ADVISORY] getCacheStatusByCredentialIds runs a groupBy filtering CalendarCache on credentialId, a column with no index in the model (this diff's migration adds only the updatedAt column, and Prisma creates no index for relation FK columns), forcing a sequential scan of the entire table. Every connected-calendars settings page load scans every CalendarCache row across all tenants (one row per cached free-busy window per credential), so page latency and database load grow with global table size rather than with the requesting user's own data.

[ADVISORY] deleteCacheHandler calls prisma.calendarCache.deleteMany directly instead of going through ICalendarCacheRepository.deleteManyByCredential, opening a parallel write path outside the repository seam whose mock guards the calendar-cache-disabled mode. Any future repository-level behavior (tenant scoping, cache-invalidation hooks, disabled-mode guards) silently will not apply to this endpoint, and cache-disabled deployments still perform real deletes against the table the disabled mode is supposed to leave untouched.

[ADVISORY] The ownership failure is thrown as a plain Error("Credential not found or access denied") instead of a TRPCError with an UNAUTHORIZED/FORBIDDEN code. tRPC wraps unknown errors as INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR, so a user attempting to delete cache for a credential they do not own produces a 500 that monitoring counts as a server fault rather than the 4xx client error the condition represents, and the client cannot distinguish it from a genuine server failure.

[ADVISORY] The allSelectedCalendars select is widened with updatedAt and googleChannelId (mirrored in the UserWithCalendars type in getConnectedDestinationCalendars.ts) but no code in this diff consumes either field, so the internal Google push-notification channel identifier rides along in every connectedCalendars response row. Web and platform-atom clients now receive internal webhook channel IDs and extra payload per calendar that no feature uses, and the UserWithCalendars type change forces every producer of that type to select these columns for fields that are dead weight.

[ADVISORY] The cache timestamp is rendered with a hardcoded Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", ...) and no timeZone option (browser-default timezone) while every other string in the component is localized through useLocale(). Non-English users see US-formatted dates in an otherwise fully localized settings page, and the time is displayed in the browser's timezone rather than the profile timezone the app standardizes on elsewhere (the same concern the codebase surfaces via timezone_mismatch_tooltip).

[ADVISORY] sed -i '' -E uses the macOS/BSD in-place idiom that GNU sed rejects (the detached empty-string argument is consumed as an empty script, so the substitution never runs), while the script unconditionally prints its success line. Linux developers running the webhook test see "✅ Updated GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL" while ../.env is silently left unchanged, so Google webhook delivery points at a stale or absent tunnel URL with no error surfaced.

[BUG] deleteCacheHandler authorizes exclusively via `userId: user.id` while CredentialActionsDropdown deliberately renders the delete-cache action for rows flagged `delegationCredentialId` or `disableConnectionModification` (the credential the viewer cannot disconnect/modify), so the component's serving assumption and the handler's ownership model were never reconciled. Any user shown the new 'Delete cached data' action on a managed/delegated/org-installed Google credential whose credential row is not owned by ctx.user (userId null or another owner) clicks 'Yes, delete cache' and receives the 'Error deleting cache' toast every single time — the mutation throws a plain Error (surfaced as a 500-class INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR rather than a 4xx) and the cache is never deleted; the feature is dead on exactly the rows it was designed to serve.

[ADVISORY] The `SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {})` touch writes a timestamp that nothing in this artifact reads — the shipped cache-status feature reads `CalendarCache.updatedAt` via `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` — so it is leftover scaffolding from a superseded iteration of the objective (SelectedCalendar-based timestamps). Every expired-cache availability refresh on the booking hot path now performs an extra unconditional multi-row UPDATE bumping `SelectedCalendar.updatedAt` for all of the credential's calendars with zero readers in the feature, silently mutating a shared column that any existing consumer (sync/watch-health logic) also observes, and the next maintainer must reverse-engineer whether this write is load-bearing before touching it.

[ADVISORY] `updatedAt` and `googleChannelId` are newly selected into the user-with-calendars query and typed into `UserWithCalendars` (getConnectedDestinationCalendars.ts), but no code in this artifact consumes them — the dropdown reads only `cacheUpdatedAt` — dead plumbing from the same superseded design. Every caller of this user query now fetches two extra columns that flow into the tRPC payload unused; since no pre-existing consumer could have read fields that were never selected before, these additions are provably readerless, and the abandoned SelectedCalendar-based design stays indistinguishable from live code for the next maintainer.

[ADVISORY] connectedCalendarsHandler hard-instantiates `new CalendarCacheRepository()` and calls `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` directly, bypassing the calendar-cache enabled/disabled selection that the mock added in this same diff exists to provide ('Skipping getCacheStatusByCredentialIds due to calendar-cache being disabled'). Deployments running with calendar cache disabled still execute the prisma `calendarCache.groupBy` on every calendars-settings load, and the mock's disabled-mode branch for this method can never execute — the disabled-mode contract is silently broken and the next cache-plumbing change must remember this direct instantiation.

[ADVISORY] deleteCacheHandler re-implements cache deletion with raw `prisma.calendarCache.deleteMany` even though `CalendarCacheRepository.deleteManyByCredential` already exists on the repository interface for exactly this operation, creating a parallel hand-maintained deletion path. Any change to cache-deletion semantics (honoring the calendar-cache disabled mode, clearing related state, switching data stores) lands in the repository but not in this handler, so users' 'Delete cached data' silently diverges from the repository contract and the two implementations must be updated in lockstep.

[ADVISORY] The cache timestamp is rendered through a hardcoded `new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", ...)` inside a component that localizes every other string via useLocale. Every non-en-US user sees US-formatted dates (e.g. 'Last updated: 7/15/2025, 3:04 PM') inside an otherwise translated string — the app's localization guarantee is silently broken on this new surface and future locale work must hunt down this hardcoded format.

[ADVISORY] The new deleteCache mutation — its ownership check, deleteMany, and route registration — plus the new `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` groupBy ship with no test anywhere in this diff. A regression dropping `userId: user.id` from the credential filter would let any authed viewer wipe another user's or team's cached availability by guessing credentialId and nothing in CI would fail; the delegation/managed-credential authorization class that this very handler mishandles shipped unnoticed precisely because nothing exercises these paths.

[BUG] The read-only 'Cache Status' block is rendered as a Radix `DropdownMenuItem`, which closes the menu on click and on Enter by default, so the non-interactive info entry behaves as a broken action. Users who click the status text (or keyboard users pressing Enter while it is focused) have the dropdown close under them, destroying the content they were trying to read; the info row also carries menu-item ARIA semantics announcing an action where none exists.

[ADVISORY] The disconnect flow (viewer.credentials.delete mutation, confirmation dialog, toasts, and cache invalidations) is reimplemented inline here while the existing DisconnectIntegration component is left exported after its call sites in SelectedCalendarsSettingsWebWrapper were removed in this diff. Credential deletion now exists in two hand-maintained copies, so the next change to disconnect behavior (extra cleanup, changed confirm copy, new invalidations) lands in one and the settings page silently diverges from every other page that disconnects apps; the retained old component also lingers as an untracked duplicate.

[BUG] The authorization-failure path throws a bare Error instead of a TRPCError, so an expected not-found/not-owned request is reported as an internal server fault rather than a 4xx. Any user who invokes viewer.calendars.deleteCache for a credential that fails the userId-scoped findFirst (e.g. a team-owned or delegation-backed credential surfaced by the same UI, or a nonexistent id) receives an HTTP 500 INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR instead of a NOT_FOUND/FORBIDDEN TRPCError; these routine denials pollute 5xx alerting/Sentry for operators and the client cannot distinguish an authz denial from a genuine outage.

[ADVISORY] The new updateManyByCredentialId call is placed at method level in getAvailability, outside the cache-guard block, so every Google availability computation issues an UPDATE against all SelectedCalendar rows for the credential — including on deployments where calendar-cache is disabled. Booking-page availability traffic (the app's hottest read path) now generates a write per check for every Google-connected user even when the cache-status feature is disabled, adding DB write load with zero feature benefit, and it redefines SelectedCalendar.updatedAt as 'last availability check' while this same PR selects that field into user-facing data via UserRepository/getConnectedDestinationCalendars.

[BUG] sed -i '' -E is BSD/macOS-only syntax: GNU sed (Linux) consumes the empty string as the script argument and then tries to open the substitution expression as an input file, so the in-place .env edit fails. On Linux the script dies with 'sed: can't read s|...|' after it has already started the tunnel, leaving tmole running while GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL is never updated in .env, so the developer's Google webhook tests silently point at the stale webhook URL.

[ADVISORY] The new SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {}) call sits outside the cache-miss guard (after the closing brace of the fetch-and-store block), so it issues an UPDATE round-trip against selectedCalendar on every availability-check invocation — cache hits included — with an empty payload whose result nothing in this PR reads. Every Google availability check on the booking-page hot path (the highest-traffic server path) gains an unconditional DB write for data no consumer uses, and because the touch runs even when the cache served the request, SelectedCalendar.updatedAt records 'last availability check' rather than the 'cache refreshed at' meaning the code comment claims — so any future reader of that timestamp gets falsely-fresh values after cache hits.

[BUG] The not-found/access-denied branch throws a plain Error instead of a tRPC TRPCError, so the deleteCache mutation returns INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR with a production-masked message for a routine authorization miss. A user who hits this guard (credential already removed in another session, or a credential the caller does not own) receives a 500-class internal error instead of a 403/404, the 'Credential not found or access denied' message never reaches the client, and server error-rate metrics and stack traces record an expected condition as an internal failure.

[BUG] The env update uses macOS-only `sed -i '' -E` syntax and the script never checks sed's exit status before printing '✅ Updated GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL', so on GNU/Linux the substitution fails while the script reports success. A developer on a Linux machine runs the webhook tester, the sed invocation fails (GNU sed treats '' as an empty script and the pattern as a filename), GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL keeps the stale tunnel URL, and the success message sends them into a long session of webhook tests that never reach the new tunnel.

[ADVISORY] The cache timestamp is formatted with a hardcoded new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", ...) instead of the active locale the component already obtains from useLocale. Every non-US user of this localized settings UI sees a US-formatted date (month/day/year, 12-hour clock) inconsistent with the locale-aware t()-translated labels surrounding it in the same dropdown, defeating the component's own i18n usage.

[ADVISORY] The cache-status display is rendered as a DropdownMenuItem — a focusable element announced as an actionable menu item — with no onClick/onSelect handler. Keyboard and screen-reader users traversing the menu land on a dead 'Cache Status' entry that is focusable and announced as a menu item but performs no action on activation, placing a non-actionable stop between the trigger and the real destructive actions.

[ADVISORY] The handler instantiates the concrete CalendarCacheRepository directly (new CalendarCacheRepository()) for the new status query, so the disabled-mode CalendarCacheRepositoryMock — which this same PR extends with a []-returning getCacheStatusByCredentialIds to encode 'no cache status when calendar-cache is disabled' — is never consulted on this path. Deployments with calendar-cache disabled still query the real calendarCache table on every connectedCalendars fetch, so residual rows (e.g., written before the feature was turned off) surface the Cache Status / Delete-cached-data UI for a feature ops deliberately disabled, and the disabled-mode contract the mock was written to enforce is silently unenforced for the new read path.

[ADVISORY] The mutation reimplements cache deletion with raw prisma.calendarCache.deleteMany instead of the repository operation ICalendarCacheRepository.deleteManyByCredential, whose mock contractually skips deletion when calendar-cache is disabled. In cache-disabled deployments the user-facing delete still performs live deletes against the calendarCache table, violating the repository-layer disabled-mode semantics every other cache write/delete path honors and leaving two parallel deletion implementations (repository method vs raw prisma) that will drift on the next schema or soft-delete change.

[ADVISORY] The newly selected updatedAt and googleChannelId fields — together with the matching UserWithCalendars type widening in getConnectedDestinationCalendars.ts that adds the same two fields to both Pick types — are consumed by nothing in this PR, because the cache-status feature reads CalendarCache.updatedAt via the repository, not SelectedCalendar.updatedAt. Every query on this repository path now fetches two dead columns and maintainers must keep three coordinated additions (user.ts select, two Pick entries, and the CalendarService touch) in sync with schema changes for data no code path reads; deleting these additions changes no observable behavior, making them pure deletion opportunities now rather than drift-prone vestiges of a superseded design.

[ADVISORY] The added `await SelectedCalendarRepository.updateManyByCredentialId(this.credential.id, {})` bumps `SelectedCalendar.updatedAt` with an empty update payload on every completion of this availability fetch-and-cache method, but nothing in this diff reads `SelectedCalendar.updatedAt` — the cache-status display reads `CalendarCache.updatedAt` via `getCacheStatusByCredentialIds` — so the write targets a table the feature never surfaces. [BUG] ENV_FILE is the CWD-relative path `../.env`, which resolves to the repository's .env only when the script is invoked from inside the scripts/ directory; invoked the natural way from the repo root (`./scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh`) it points at the directory above the checkout. Run from the repo root, the script `touch`-creates `<repo-parent>/.env` and writes GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL into a file no process reads, while still printing the ✅ success message (line 73); the dev server never receives the tunnel URL, Google channel registrations keep pointing at the previous value, and the developer gets zero error output explaining why webhook testing doesn't work — plus a stray .env file is left polluting the parent directory.

adjudication.rationale: In `scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh`, `ENV_FILE` is set to a CWD-relative path (`ENV_FILE="../.env"`). Since the script does not `cd` to its own directory, invoking it from the repo root (`./scripts/test-gcal-webhooks.sh`) makes `../.env` resolve to the parent of the repo, not the repo’s `.env`. The script then `touch`-creates that wrong file and writes `GOOGLE_WEBHOOK_URL=...` into it while still printing a success message, so the intended `.env` used by the dev server is not updated and webhook testing can silently fail, leaving a stray `.env` outside the repo.
